I am aware that it is common for a democracy to have anonymity when voting. This is not a democracy. This site is, it seems, also about accountability. While this is a big step and potentially a drastic step, I think that it should be given due consideration. Hear me out and I will try to explain my reasoning...

I was poking and prodding, as I am wont to do, in a thread about Mrs. Clinton. I saw a perfectly rational post that had been given a single, solitary, down voat. Try as I might, I could not think of a reason for anyone to have marked it as such. Then I thought about it some more.

With the brigading, the sock puppets, and the general jackassery that we, as a community, seem to be fond of there is a simple solution. It will not prevent anything. It will, on the other hand, provide evidence and enable people to make their own judgments. All we need to do is enable a "who voated" link next to the voat buttons. Then you can see who has done what and check to see how they have voated in the past. Voats would become public information and those voating would have to consent to that.

So, not only would we be able to see who voated what on a specific comment or submission but we'd also be able to see a person's profile and be able to review their voat history.

Voting, in the real world, is often not anonymous at all. If you have ever been to a town meeting or a public referendum then you know that voting is done with a show or hands or via verbal acknowledgement. You see this in everything from the UN to your local school council. Voting, and thus voating, does not demand anonymity. In fact, being accountable for your votes has been a historical significance since the days of early Greece.

This will not stop anything - though it may curtail some behaviors. What it will do is provide opacity for those willing to spend the time looking. I think that it may make sense to try this. As it would simply be pulling from the database it is unlikely to cause an undue overhead. This is not a panacea but it is, potentially, a step in the right direction and I think it may make sense to give this a trial run to see the results. There is some potential that it will change a lot of things if we know we are accountable for our comments and our voats.

I've been pondering and trying to come up with an amicable solution and, frankly, this is the best I have come up with so far. Obviously, I welcome comments, suggestions, feedback, criticism, and any ideas that further this. The idea of anonymity in voating really does not jive entirely with an open democracy. It was enacted so that people could not be forced to vote in a specific manner by those who have power over them. This is the internet, such is unlikely to be needed and there are myriad examples of public voting being successful and normal.

Thoughts?

Edit: I had checked to see if anyone had posited this idea already but, somehow, I missed the glaringly obvious post and a very well written submission at that. So, allow me to also link to that one here: https://voat.co/v/ideasforvoat/comments/433455

That post was made by @nomerasques and brings some other things to mind as well as touching on the historical aspects. While we should merge the two, that seems impossible and I am loathe to delete a thread that has comments in it already and will not do so. My sincere apologies if this this creates any difficulties. I encourage interested persons to pay attention to and comment in both threads.

This repeats a prior post, so I'm going to copy my comment from that thread:

It might seem like a good idea at first, but there are some worrying negatives: public voting records would make users less comfortable voting how they want to for fear of being audited (porn, for example). Witch hunts are already a problem; having access to someone's voting record would add fuel to the fire. It strips away a level of privacy for very little tangible gain, which is a problem in itself. It would be much easier for an individual or corporation to build a profile on your user account. It could lead to users trying to use each other's records to discredit a comment (ad hominem) which we see enough of with comment records already.

I'm happy with my comments being public, but I think upvotes and downvoats are too personal a thing to make public. At that point you're not looking at what I say about an issue, but looking directly at what I think. I should always have the choice of keeping my thoughts private.

If you're unwilling to open your beliefs up to scrutiny then how strongly do you feel about those beliefs? If you're unable and unwilling to stand up for your beliefs should you be voting? I am not entirely sure how to answer those questions but I think transparency will have many benefits including encouraging people to think about and reason their way to solid core beliefs and give them the courage to back them up. Current system info: 90Gal, 40Gal sump, skimmer off, Fuge lit, 'live sand' from BRS (80lbs), Reefsaver rock from BRS (100lbs), 2x 8x8x4 Biofilter Bricks. 3lbs LR rubble from trusted LFS.

When I set up my most recent tank I waited 2 month before starting my algae scrubber. I wasn't confident there would be enough nutrients in the water for it to thrive. Great question, I look forward reading other opinions.
i have been told as much ,but also been told that the sooner one starts the better.

I'd say now. First of all, chaeto is dirt cheap and you can pick up a ton of it from any other hobbyist out there for free or almost free. As long as you monitor it and make sure there isn't any large die-off (and if there is you remove the dead stuff regularly) the benefits out way the risk. First it helps impregnate your tank with healthy bacteria from a established system. This will help speed up your cycle and stabilize your tank earlier. It'll absorb some (I really do mean some, don't take this as a excuse to skip regular maintenance) of the excess nutrients and help soften up spikes in nutrients from die-off or any other adverse factors. Not only that, if you get algae with critters in it, it'll provide food for them while your tank gets up to speed. This way also your chaeto grows with your tank so you wont have get a fuck ton of it.

Edit: just as a caution, I wouldn't dump a shit ton in there at once. Put in a small amount into your sump. See how it reacts and then add more slowly.
